title: U.S. Regulator Grants Bank Charter to Trump-Backed World Liberty Financial
excerpt: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency conditionally approved a national trust charter for the Trump family's crypto venture, allowing it to directly issue its USD1 stablecoin and custody reserves under federal supervision.
body:
• The OCC on Friday conditionally approved World Liberty Trust Company's application for a national trust charter, allowing the Trump-linked crypto firm to issue, custody, and manage reserves for its USD1 stablecoin
  • USD1 is currently the fourth-largest stablecoin by market cap at approximately $4 billion, and the Trump family has earned an estimated $50 million from the stablecoin through June 2026
  • The charter requires maintaining at least $20 million in capital; Eric Trump signed a passivity agreement pledging not to influence bank operations
  • Democrats have called the approval a major conflict of interest, with Senator Elizabeth Warren describing it as "unprecedented crypto corruption" that has "metastasized to the banking system"

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on Friday conditionally approved a federal bank charter for World Liberty Trust Company, the banking arm of President Donald Trump's crypto venture World Liberty Financial — a decision that expands the first family's financial empire deeper into the regulated banking system.

The conditional preliminary approval, disclosed in a letter on the OCC's website, grants World Liberty Trust a national trust charter that it applied for in January. The charter would allow the firm to directly issue its USD1 stablecoin, custody the U.S. dollar assets backing it, and settle payments — functions currently handled by business partner BitGo.

What the Charter Allows

Unlike a traditional bank charter, a national trust charter does not generally permit deposit-taking or lending. Instead, it allows crypto companies to hold assets on behalf of clients nationwide under a single federal regulator, provide settlement and asset servicing, and court institutional customers including cryptocurrency exchanges, market makers, and investment firms.

https://x.com/blek5000/status/2088430989055754698

"A national trust bank brings USD1 issuance, custody, and reserve management together under OCC supervision, examined on the same standards that have governed banks for generations," said Zach Witkoff, World Liberty Trust's president and chairman, in a statement.

"We welcome continuous scrutiny from Federal regulators for many years to come."

— Zach Witkoff, President and Chairman, World Liberty Trust Company

Deep Trump Family Ties

World Liberty Financial's leadership is deeply intertwined with both the Trump family and the Witkoff family, longtime Trump allies. The firm was co-founded by Trump and his three sons in late 2024. Zach Witkoff is the son of Steve Witkoff, Trump's special diplomatic envoy. Robert Witkoff, Steve's brother, will serve as a bank director.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=r8r6utFVOMM

The venture has been enormously lucrative for the Trumps. Reuters estimates the family earned approximately $50 million from the USD1 stablecoin alone through June 2026. Overall, World Liberty Financial has funneled more than $1.6 billion to the president and his family as of April, according to Reuters calculations. USD1 has grown to become the fourth-largest stablecoin by market capitalization, at around $4 billion.

Conflict of Interest Concerns

The approval is certain to intensify political backlash. Democrats have argued that a bank charter for a Trump-owned business reviewed by a regulator who serves at the president's pleasure represents an unprecedented conflict of interest.

Senator Elizabeth Warren, ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee, has been the most vocal critic. "President Trump's unprecedented crypto corruption has metastasized to the banking system," she said when the OCC began its review. "The OCC's review is a sham."

In February, two Democratic senators asked Trump's Treasury secretary to examine the national security implications of a reported $500 million stake purchased by a figure linked to the United Arab Emirates' national security adviser.

The OCC pushed back on the criticism, noting in its approval letter that the application was reviewed by career staff and that Comptroller Jonathan Gould "acted consistently with their statutory duties and ethical obligations." The charter includes conditions: maintaining at least $20 million in capital, hiring a qualified internal audit manager, and notifying the regulator of major business plan changes. Eric Trump signed a passivity agreement pledging not to influence bank operations.

Industry Context

World Liberty is not the first crypto firm to receive such a charter. Circle, Ripple, BitGo, Fidelity Digital Assets, and Paxos have all received preliminary approval under Comptroller Gould. The GENIUS Act, signed by Trump last July, established the first major regulatory framework for stablecoins, opening the door for these applications.

The approval positions World Liberty to compete directly with established stablecoin issuers by bringing issuance, custody, and conversion under one federally supervised roof — a "full-stack offering" that could attract major institutional clients seeking regulatory clarity in the crypto space.
